| Source | Cost | Attribution required | Monetized use OK | Account needed | Formats | Risk notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube Audio Library (SFX) | Free | No for standard-license tracks; yes for Creative Commons tracks | Yes | NOT VERIFIED (lives in YouTube Studio) | NOT VERIFIED | Only source YouTube itself calls copyright-safe |
| Pixabay | Free | No | Yes | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | No standalone redistribution; shield-icon music tracks are in Content ID |
| Freesound | Free | Depends on license: CC0 no, BY yes | CC0 and BY yes; BY-NC and Sampling+ no | Yes | NOT VERIFIED | Check the license of every sound; Content ID false claims are possible |
| Mixkit | Free | No | Yes, YouTube named explicitly | No | NOT VERIFIED | Full license text not readable; restrictions come from the User Terms |
| Sonniss GDC bundles | Free | No | Yes | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | No redistribution as sound effects; no AI training |
| Zapsplat | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | Official site returned 403 on every page |
| BBC Sound Effects | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED (secondary sources say no) | NOT VERIFIED | NOT VERIFIED | Treat as not usable until the licence is read |
| Roblox Creator Store audio / "oof" | n/a | n/a | NOT VERIFIED | n/a | n/a | Docs frame use as on-platform only; no off-platform grant found |

## 1. YouTube Audio Library
URL opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3376882?hl=en
- **Copyright-safe:** "Music and sound effects from the YouTube Audio Library are copyright-safe."
- **Content ID:** "Copyright-safe music and sound effects downloaded from the Audio Library won't be claimed by a rights holder"
- **Monetization:** "If you're in the YouTube Partner Program, you can monetize videos with music and sound effects from the Audio Library."
- **Attribution:** "If you're using a track with a Creative Commons license, you must credit the artist in your video's description." The page also refers to "a standard YouTube Audio Library license that doesn't require attribution".
- **Caveat:** "Only music and sound effects from the Audio Library are known to YouTube to be copyright-safe."
- The page has no sentence on a license specific to sound effects; the attribution wording is written about music tracks.

## 2. Pixabay
URLs opened: https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/ , https://pixabay.com/service/terms/ , https://pixabay.com/service/faq/
- **Attribution (summary):** "Use Content without having to attribute the author (although giving credit is always appreciated by our community!)"
- **Commercial use (terms, section 5):** "royalty-free right to download, use, copy, modify or adapt" / "the Content for commercial or non-commercial purposes ('Content License')."
- **Audio is covered (terms, section 2):** "Audio", which means music, sounds, sound effects and other audio representations and content.
- **Standalone ban (summary):** "You cannot sell or distribute Content (either in digital or physical form) on a Standalone basis."
- **Standalone defined:** "Standalone means where no creative effort has been applied to the Content"
- **Other bans (summary):** "You cannot use Content in a misleading or deceptive way." and "You cannot use any of the Content as part of a trade-mark, design-mark, trade-name, business name or service mark."
- **Content ID (FAQ):** "Tracks displaying a shield icon are registered with Content ID and may trigger claims, which can usually be disputed using the _Download certificate_"
- **Binding text:** the summary says "only the full Content License is legally binding."

## 3. Freesound
URL opened: https://freesound.org/help/faq/
- **Licenses listed:** "zero (cc0): http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/", "attribution (by): http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/", "attribution noncommercial (by-nc): http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/"
- **Legacy license:** "In freesound "1" we had an additional license called Sampling+:"
- **CC0:** "for the "zero" license you can do pretty much what you want with the sound."
- **BY:** "For "attribution" you should always mention the original creators of the sounds when you use them."
- **BY-NC:** "you can't earn any money with the piece of work you create!" This rules it out for a monetized channel.
- **Sampling+:** "you can do pretty much what you could do with the attribution noncommercial license" and "you can't make commercial advertisement with the sound." Avoid it.
- **General warning:** "Some sounds you cannot use commercially, and many of the sounds you need to credit the author."
- **Recommended credit format:** "This [video/theatre piece/...] uses these sounds from freesound: "sound1" by user1 ( http://freesound.org/s/soundID/ )" / ""sound2", "sound3" by user2 ( http://freesound.org/people/user2/ ) licensed under CCBY 4.0 etc.."
- **Account:** "To download a sound, first make sure you are logged into your registered account."
- **Content ID:** "This is an unfortunate consequence of systems such as YouTube Content ID Scanning." and "Most often this can be (and has been) resolved by disputing the copyright claim through YouTube"
- Freesound also keeps a per-user attribution list at https://freesound.org/home/attribution/ (needs login; not opened).

- https://create.roblox.com/docs/audio/assets : Creator Store audio is "made by Roblox and the Roblox community for creators to use within their games", "including more than 100,000 professionally-produced sound effects and music tracks from top audio and music partners."
- Same page: "reuse them in any project on the platform."
- https://create.roblox.com/docs/production/creator-store : distributed assets are "for others to use within their own game development."

Neither page states an explicit ban on off-platform use, and neither grants it. Nothing was found on the "oof" or classic Roblox sounds specifically. The safe guidance is not to rip Roblox or Creator Store audio into Shorts and to use a sound-alike from the verified sources above.
